textPresets.name: Setup: local monitors
textPresets.text:
Local monitors need no selection: every preset subscribes to subsystem:MonitoringManager.findLocalMonitor(...) on the Director Companion is connected to.

Shown: FPS (latest, 10-sample and 60-sample average), GPU profiler frame time (Total, Compositor, GUI, Render Everything, DMX, Video Upload, Capture Upload) in ms, CPU Total (unit stated as ms by the help site; live on r34.0.3 the graph reports yUnits = "Units", so treat the number as relative), GPU memory (MB), Designer process memory (MB) and the "Machine" health monitor percentages (CPU/GPU time, CPU/GPU memory, Disk; source: disguise's official Grafana dashboard; values confirmed live on r34.0.3 in the 0-100 range).

Also included after the r34.0.3 live run: Disk read/write MB/s (the developer guide calls Disk over LiveUpdate work in progress, but the values arrive), monitor and series name discovery, GPU thresholds, FPS min/max and graph categories.

Update rate: monitoring class (default 1000 ms). Never set 0: monitors push every frame. Colour rules assume a 60 Hz project: red when FPS falls 10 below (latest) or 5 below (averages), GPU Total >= 17 ms, Machine % >= 80.

textPresets.name: Setup: remote monitors
textPresets.text:
Set the selection selHost to the hostname of the remote Designer machine WITHOUT the ":d3" suffix (the presets append it, e.g. selHost = ACTOR01 -> "ACTOR01:d3"). Hostname case sensitivity is undocumented: copy it exactly as shown in d3Net / the "Remote nodes list" preset.

Shown: remote FPS (latest and 10-sample average), whether that remote fps graph has expired (stopped receiving data) and the list of remote nodes the MonitoringManager knows (discovery aid for selHost).

Also included after the live run: remote Machine CPU/GPU time, GPU/CPU totals, GPU memory and the per-node monitor name list.

Open points: only "fps" is documented as a remote monitor name; whether the Director must first mark the remote graph in use (MonitoringManager.useMonitorByName) is untested. A wrong selHost produces a LiveUpdate error; the module backs off before retrying.

textPresets.name: Transport State: setup
textPresets.text:
Object path for every preset in this category: transportManager:default (Designer's default transport manager; no selection needed). Readouts: playhead in beats (equals seconds at 60 bpm), play mode as string and as state enum, playing / stopped / holding flags, play-to-end and loop-section modes, track loaded, playback speed, current track name and length, section count, timecode chase and source status strings, incoming timecode and pre-roll countdown. Controls: master brightness and volume (readout, +/-5 % nudges with rotary support, FULL / ZERO / MUTE), ENGAGE / DISENGAGE and a one-button Engaged toggle (Toggle Disguise Boolean action). Values with state colours use the LiveUpdate Compare feedback. Transport commands (play, stop, cue, section navigation) are not available over LiveUpdate: pair this module with companion-module-disguise-osc or the REST Transport API.

Also included after the live run: track position and timecode position strings, free-running flag, BPM at playhead, section index, current / next section names, section elapsed and remaining (beats), set-list track names, active layer count and the GUI playhead. Still experimental (99): the timecode source name and the playhead of a named transport (the test project has one transport and no timecode source).

textPresets.name: Setup: Track & Layer
textPresets.text: Create these selection variables before adding presets from this category: selTrack = track name as shown in Designer (quoted automatically, e.g. Track 1); selLayer = layer name inside that track (Layer editor name, e.g. Video 1); selSection = 0-based section index for the section presets; selBeat = a track beat (float) for the note/beat presets; selLayerIndex = 0-based position in the track layer list for the "(by index)" presets. Readouts show: track name/length/BPM, section and layer counts, section start/end, note at beat, beat-to-time, cue count, TC adjust, and per-layer name / enabled / live / start / end / length / anchored plus the key-0 values of pos.x, pos.y, scale and brightness. Readouts are grey; the TC-adjust knob presets (amber) write to Designer. All values are track beats unless labelled time. Also included after the live run: layer name list, section table / note / length / start (s), section of a beat, cue tags at a beat, the cue table (beat, note, section flag), layer extents / crashed / dormant / fields / key times, patched brightness, brightness at a beat, all pos.x keys and the video key-0 resource. Still experimental (99): the text key (needs a Text layer).

textPresets.name: Setup: Layer Control
textPresets.text: Requires selection variable(s) selTrack and selLayer (and selLayerIndex for the "(by index)" presets), see 05 Track & Layer. Presets: layer enable (green) / disable (red) / toggle, layer start and length nudges and sets (amber), keyframe key-0 nudges and sets for pos.x, pos.y, scale and brightness (amber, "(knob)" presets also drive rotary left/right when rotaryActions is on), brightness = 0 black, and brightness "constant" on/off (disableSequencing). Each control also subscribes to its own value so the button shows the live number. Anchored layers reject start/length changes; only key 0 is changed, later keyframes still play. Sets are persistent and undoable in Designer.

textPresets.name: Stage & Screen setup
textPresets.text: Create these selection variable(s) in Companion before dropping the presets: selScreen = exact Designer name of the Surface (Screen2), e.g. Surface 1 (the presets add the quotes); selProjector = projector name, e.g. projector 1; selScreenUid = UID of any display copied from its editor title bar (right-click > Copy UID), including the 0x prefix - the "Display (UID)" presets work for LED and DMX screens too. Readouts: name, mesh, resolution, health flags, offset/rotation/scale (m / deg), master fade, hold, render layer, alpha, blend mode, tracking state; projector feed/output/shutter/blend/feather. Controls (amber = write, green = on/enable, red = off/hold): offset X/Y/Z +-0.1 m and reset, master fade +-0.05 / 1.0 / 0.0, hold ON/OFF/toggle, ON/OFF stage, external update ON/OFF, projector render mode, shutter OPEN/CLOSE, dynamic blend ON/OFF, feather +-0.05. Sets are undoable in Designer and persist in the project. Nudge presets also respond to rotary encoders (right = +, left = -). Also included after the live run: the projectors of a surface, the surfaces of a projector, LED screen name / fade / hold / offset (selection selLedScreen = LED screen name) and stage display count / dynamic blend (selection selStageUid = Stage UID, hex with 0x prefix). Still experimental (99): DMX screen rows (no DMX screen in the test project) and the stage venue name (no venue assigned).

textPresets.name: EV setup: custom variables
textPresets.text: Expression Variables device readouts. Create these selection variables first: selEvUid = the device UID as an unquoted hex literal (Designer: right-click the Expression Variables device editor title bar > Copy UID, e.g. 0x0123456789abcdef); selEvIndex = zero-based row index of the variable in the device editor (plain integer, no quotes; rows can be drag-reordered so re-check after edits). Presets in this category read the i-th variable through getByUID(selEvUid).container.variables[selEvIndex]: defaultFloat (value of a Float variable), defaultString (value of a String variable), name and type (0 Float, 1 String, 2 Function). All rows are read-only: the pyi setter exists but a LiveUpdate set through the list subscript is untested, so nudge/set knobs are deferred until the live test. Experimental rows (see 99 Experimental) additionally need selEvDevice (device name = filename part of objects/ExpressionVariablesDevice/<name>.apx), selEvName (variable name, case-sensitive) and selEvLayer (name of an ExpressionVariables layer currently under the playhead). None of the Expression Variables rows could be checked live: the test project has no Expression Variables device.

textPresets.name: RenderStream setup
textPresets.text: RenderStream presets read subsystem:RenderStreamSystem (cluster/instance health, per-node flags, receive statuses, active latency) and Machine takeover. Create these selection variables first: selWorkload = workload ID as a Python int - copy it from the Cluster Workload widget ('Copy UID') or from REST GET /api/session/renderstream/layers then GET /api/session/renderstream/layerstatus?uid=<layer uid> (workload.uid); if the copied value is hex, enter it as 0x...; selInstance = zero-based instance index inside the workload (0 = first render node); selMachine = render node / machine name exactly as shown in the Cluster Workload widget Instances > Machine column. The 'RS workload layer count' preset shows how many layers carry a workload (on r34.0.3 the id map itself serialises empty, so read ids through the RS Layer Workload ID preset). The layer-route presets (RS Layer ...) need selTrack (track name) and selRsLayer (zero-based index of the RenderStream layer among the track's RenderStream leaf layers); the RS Layer Workload ID preset shows the workload id as text ready for selWorkload. The aggregate rows (node summary, running count, any dropping / down, health list, min FPS, max latency, dropped total, all subscribed, last errors, status messages) were verified live with a workload that had no running instances. All RenderStream rows are read-only; workload start/stop/restart is only available through the REST session API, not LiveUpdate. While a workload has no running instances the per-instance rows show PATH_ERROR (the Director answers "out of range error accessing workload instance"); the module backs off and retries on its own.

textPresets.name: Setup: Failover & d3Net
textPresets.text: These presets read the failover / d3Net state of ONE machine addressed by name. Create the selection variables selMachine and set it to the machine's resource name exactly as it appears in Designer's d3Net Manager / Machines list (the 'name' field of GET /api/session/status/health - not necessarily the Windows hostname). Every preset here uses the object path Machine:"$(liveupdate:selMachine)"; change the selection variable(s) and all presets re-point at once (duplicate the page and use a second selection variable(s) if you need two machines side by side). Readouts: taken over a failed machine (understudy side), failed (actor side), auto failover disabled, network connected, network status code, active, role, running as, understudy targets, plus identity: machine name, hostname, IP, hardware type, d3Net node id, GUI visible, resource status. There are deliberately NO write presets in this category: role, hostname, director and understudy targets reconfigure the session, and the fail / restore machine commands are not reachable through LiveUpdate set (use REST POST /api/session/failover/failovermachine and /restoremachine). Alarm colours: add the liveUpdateCompare feedback as noted per preset (red = failed / offline / taken over / inactive, amber = auto failover disabled). Rows for the connected machine itself, the acting director, offline / failed / taken-over lists across the whole d3Net, understudy configuration, the failover timeout, network adaptors and by-hostname addressing (selection selHost, shared with 03 Monitoring Remote) were verified live and are included. Only the name of the Director's understudy stays experimental (no understudy in the test project). Values update at the state (500 ms) or static (5000 ms) rate; failover indicators are method calls that the Director may evaluate on every cycle, so do not lower them below the defaults.

textPresets.name: Setup: selections & settings
textPresets.text: LiveUpdate can READ and SET Designer properties; it cannot issue transport commands (play, stop, cue, section navigation). Pair this module with companion-module-disguise-osc or the REST Transport API for commands. Presets address show objects through the module's own selection variables ($(liveupdate:selTrack), $(liveupdate:selScreen),...). Set them once in the connection settings (section "Selections") or from a button with the "Set selection" action; every preset that uses a selection re-subscribes automatically when it changes. Normal-tier selections: selBeat = a track beat as a number, e.g. 32; selEvIndex = 0-based row index of the variable inside the device (unquoted integer); selEvUid = UID of the Expression Variables device, hex with 0x prefix; selHost = hostname of the remote machine WITHOUT the:d3 suffix (the presets append it); selInstance = 0-based RenderStream instance index (unquoted integer); selLayer = layer name inside the selected track (selTrack), e.g. Video 1; selLayerIndex = 0-based position in the track layer list (unquoted integer) for the "(by index)" presets; selLedScreen = LED screen name; selMachine = Machine resource name exactly as listed in d3Net Manager (the same string is used for remote node lookups and RenderStream machine names; confirm on your Director); selProjector = projector name; selRsLayer = 0-based index among the track's RenderStream leaf layers; selScreen = Surface (screen2) name; selScreenUid = UID of any display, hex with 0x prefix (right-click the editor title bar > Copy UID); selSection = 0-based section index (unquoted integer); selStageUid = Stage UID, hex with 0x prefix; selTrack = track name as shown in Designer, e.g. Track 1 (quoted by the paths); selWorkload = RenderStream workload id as unquoted decimal digits (the RS Layer Workload ID preset shows it as text; also Cluster Workload widget > Copy UID or REST GET /api/session/renderstream/layerstatus). Experimental presets (category 99, names prefixed [EXP]) are hidden until the connection setting "Show experimental presets" is on; they use: selDmxScreen = DMX screen name; selEvDevice = Expression Variables device name (file name part of objects/ExpressionVariablesDevice/<name>.apx); selEvLayer = Expression Variables layer name (module: prefix); selEvName = expression variable name, case-sensitive; selTransport = transport manager name other than default. Update intervals are prefilled from the connection settings (Monitoring / Playhead / State / Static) and can be edited per button.

textPresets.name: Setup: how to use templates
textPresets.text: Templates are generic buttons with literal placeholders; they do nothing until edited (the module skips subscribing while a path still contains '<' or '>'). After dragging one: (1) open the LiveUpdate Variable feedback and replace <OBJECT_PATH> with a Designer object expression (e.g. track:"Track 1", screen2:"LED Wall", transportManager:default, subsystem:MonitoringManager.findLocalMonitor("fps")) and object.<PROPERTY_PATH> with the Python member path (e.g. object.description, object.lengthInBeats, object.player.tRender); (2) rename the variable myValue to something unique for that object/property pair (letters, digits, underscore, max 40 characters) and change every $(liveupdate:myValue) in the button text and in the actions to the new name; two buttons watching the same path must use the same variable name and the same Update Frequency; (3) keep Update Frequency above 0 (prefilled from the State interval setting, 500 ms). Set / Nudge / Toggle actions do not take paths: they write to the subscription that owns the variable name, which is why each control template carries the matching feedback. Number values are JavaScript expressions evaluated after variable substitution ($(liveupdate:myValue)+1 works; the result must be a finite number); Boolean is a checkbox; JSON is a partial object merged into the property ({"x": 0.0} changes only x of a vector); String is sent verbatim. Object, array and resource values ({uid, path, type}) arrive as JSON strings, so use jsonparse / jsonpath in expressions (see Watch: JSON field x). A readout shows ERROR or PATH_ERROR when the Director rejects the path; fix the path, the module resubscribes on its own.

textPresets.name: About experimental presets
textPresets.text: Read-only presets that could not be confirmed on the r34.0.3 test rig: it had no Expression Variables device, DMX screen, timecode source, stage venue, Text layer or second transport, and one row (RS Layer Node Status) needs a running workload instance. They may show ERROR / PATH_ERROR; that is not a module bug. Confirmed rows are promoted to their home category without changing ids or variable names (103 rows were promoted after the 2026-09-04 live run).

perDim.summary: Monitoring dimension drafted from 27 supported candidates (19 doc-verified, 8 inferred; mon-renderstream-prefetcher-names excluded as unverified). 40 rows: 21 normal-tier readouts in '02 Monitoring Local' (fps latest/avg10/avg60, GPUProfiler Total + 6 sub-series, CPU Total, GPUMemory, ProcessMemory, the five Grafana-only 'Machine' percent series and the two Grafana-only 'Disk' MB/s series - all flagged liveTestPriority high - plus the global graphs-paused flag), 6 normal-tier rows in '03 Monitoring Remote' (remote fps latest + 10-sample avg via $(custom:d3_host), remote monitor expired flag, resolved remote nodeName, MonitoringManager.remoteNodes() discovery list, Machine.nodeName via $(custom:d3_machine)), and 13 read-only experimental rows (local monitor-name / series-name / units / thresholds / raw min-max / category discovery, remote per-node monitor names, and remote Machine/GPUProfiler/CPU/GPUMemory readouts built on the inferred mon-remote-any pattern). No control rows: nothing in this dimension is a sensible Stream Deck write; the only pyi-writable members (searchString, nodeName, expired, pollInterval) are monitor configuration and were skipped or shipped read-only. Every MetricMonitor value uses the monitoring class (1000 ms), booleans the state class, discovery lists/identity strings the static class; never 0. stateColour rules follow the guide (fps error = 10 below a 60 Hz target, warning = 5 below on the smoothed series) and the Grafana thresholds (GPU 17 ms, Machine 80 %). Text templates in expression mode use the same backtick-plus-\n convention as the module's existing fpsMonitor preset.

Duplicate: the candidate itself names the failover dimension as primary owner of Machine:"<name>" / object.hasTakenOverFailedMachine(); shipping it here would create a second pair/variable for the same member (fo_ rows).
Marginal subsystem flag (verifier: 'marginal value as stated'); connection/subsystem health is covered by 01 Connection and by the readouts themselves erroring.
Pure UI configuration (Monitoring Manager search box) with no show value; it is the only write in this dimension and a LiveUpdate set on a Subsystem-rooted (non-Resource) path is undocumented.

Status unverified / verifierSupported false: 'renderstream' and 'prefetcher' are constants on _BlipValue classes that are not MetricMonitors, and two quoted series labels do not exist on the help page. Excluded by rule; RenderStream health belongs to 09 RenderStream (subsystem:RenderStreamSystem).

openQuestions: CPU 'Total' unit: the guide calls the subscription 'CPU utilisation', the help page defines the CPU graph in milliseconds, and the Grafana dashboard never subscribes to 'CPU'. monl_cpu_total ships without a unit suffix or colour rule; run monl_cpu_units (graphDescriptor(False).yUnits) and read one live value before labelling.

'Machine' (five percent series) and 'Disk' (Read/Write MB/s) are evidenced only by disguise-one's official Grafana dashboard; 'Machine' is absent from the help page's Local graph list and the guide says Disk over LiveUpdate is 'in development (DSOF-20732)'. All seven rows are liveTestPriority high - confirm they resolve on r34.0.3 and whether a disk-utilisation percent series exists.

Remote monitors: (a) does the Director need MonitoringManager.useMonitorByName(nodeName, monitorName, True) before data flows; (b) hostname case sensitivity; (c) do object.remoteNodes() strings and Machine.nodeName carry the ':d3' suffix (decides whether d3_host stays a bare hostname as the setup text assumes); (d) which monitor names other than 'fps' are published remotely (promote the monr_ experimental rows only after monr_node_monitor_names lists them).

stateColour thresholds assume a 60 Hz project (fps < 50 error, < 55 warning on averages; GPU >= 17 ms; Machine >= 80 %). The liveUpdateCompare feedback is still a proposal; if it is not implemented the rows ship as plain readouts, and if it is, consider a per-project custom variable (d3_target_fps) instead of hard-coded numbers.

Frequency: research and the critic recommended 500 ms for fps/GPU/CPU latest readouts and 1000 ms for rolling averages; the lead's class table puts every MetricMonitor value at monitoring = 1000 ms, which this draft follows. If a livelier FPS bug is wanted, lower the monitoring class default rather than mixing classes across rows of one monitor.

seriesAverage edge cases are undocumented: return value for an unknown series title, for nSamples above the FIFO capacity (fpsAvg60), and for an expired/paused monitor; also what findLocalMonitor returns for an unknown name. Combined with the module's subscribe-storm hazard, the Phase 2 guard (skip paths containing '<...>', back off after errors) should land before remote rows with a wrong d3_host are exposed.

Companion expression details to confirm on 5.0.4: the backtick template literal with a literal \n escape (copied from the module's existing fpsMonitor preset), the ternary operator used in the boolean rows, and that jsonpath(jsonparse(x), '$.Actual.min') returns a scalar for monl_fps_minmax.

Cross-dimension variable dedupe: monr_machine_node_name uses Machine:"$(custom:d3_machine)" / object.nodeName (variable machineNodeName); if the failover dimension defines the same pair the lead must keep a single variable name and frequency class for it.

Operators must create d3_workload (Python int workload id from the Cluster Workload widget 'Copy UID' or REST layerstatus workload.uid; prefix 0x if hex), d3_instance (zero-based) and d3_machine; the experimental layer route adds d3_track and a new d3_rslayer index variable. 3 candidates skipped (rs-metric-monitor unverified, rs-machine-status-by-uid ambiguous uid, rs-texture-param-receivers marginal).

skipped.reason: Status unverified (verifierSupported false): RenderStreamMetricMonitor is a _BlipValue, not a MetricMonitor, and no doc or pyi ties findLocalMonitor("renderstream") to a graph or names any series title. Excluded by rule.

Inferred, but the verifier could not establish whether the uid from GET /api/session/renderstream/pools is the RenderStreamMachine or the underlying Machine (statusString does not exist on Machine, so the row would error); there is no documented RenderStreamMachine object-path prefix and it would need a new custom variable for the uid. Outside the experimental scope set by the lead (comprehension summaries and the layer route). The same statusString is reachable through the experimental layer route row rs_exp_layer_inst_machine.

Doc-verified but marginal diagnostic: returns a list of Subscription objects whose JSON shape is undocumented (pyi body not inspected), r33.1+ only, and not something a show operator reads on a Stream Deck. The workload/stream receive statuses already cover stream health.

openQuestions: Workload ID format: the pyi types it as Python int; the LiveUpdate doc says to copy it from the Cluster Workload widget ('Copy UID') or the deprecated V1 /api/v1/renderstream/workloads, and the session swagger calls layerstatus workload.uid a uint64-as-string. Confirm whether the copied value is decimal or hex (hex needs a 0x prefix in d3_workload) and whether it equals RenderStreamModuleConfigBase.workloadId (rs_exp_layer_workload_id).

Subscribe storm on stopped workloads: every per-instance row (getWorkloadInstance(...)) presumably returns an {error} when the workload is stopped or the index is out of range (undocumented). Per INVENTORY.md section 5 the module then retries about 10 times per second on any valuesChanged. Until that module bug is fixed, operators should remove or disable RenderStream instance presets while a workload is down; the generator may want a warning in rs_setup.

JSON serialisation of _BlipValue structs (WorkloadInstance, WorkloadHealth, SubscribedStreamStatus, the getWorkloadLayers() map) is only described as 'recursive' in the doc. All jsonpath text expressions assume pyi property names appear verbatim as JSON keys and that receiver serialises as {uid,path,type}; verify on a live system and also check whether uint64 workload ids / stream handles arrive as JSON numbers (precision loss above 2^53 in Companion) or strings.

Enum meanings are undocumented for WorkloadInstance.status, WorkloadHealth.status and .priority, and getLicensingState() (only RS_AUTH_MODE_FULL = 2 named). rs_inst_status, rs_inst_health_status and rs_licensing ship as raw codes; capture values live before adding colour rules. rs_licensing uses a '!=' stateColour operator - confirm the proposed liveUpdateCompare feedback supports '!=' (and '==' on booleans) or drop that rule.

Variable-name reconciliation with 10 Failover & d3Net: machine-has-taken-over is listed in both dimensions. The pair Machine:"$(custom:d3_machine)" / object.hasTakenOverFailedMachine() must carry one variable name; this draft uses machineHasTakenOver with state class.

New custom variable d3_rslayer (zero-based index into track:"..".getLeafLayers(RenderStreamModule)) was introduced for the experimental layer route because the lead's variable list has no index for it; rename if the lead prefers another id. The verifier also notes that a class-name argument inside the object expression is not demonstrated in docs, so the whole layer route (10 rows) may need the no-argument form track:"..".getLeafLayers()[n].
Whether comprehension subscriptions that call .health() inside a list (rs_exp_health_list) push change notifications - the doc says health is computed and must be subscribed per instance.

Units of RenderStreamSystem.activeLatency() and SubscribedStreamStatus.activeLatency (frames vs seconds) are undocumented, so no latency threshold colour is shipped; likewise the min receive fps threshold is show-dependent and left to the operator.

Companion expression assumptions to confirm in the generator's live test: jsonpath() with a single match returns the scalar (wrap:false) while multiple matches return an array that template-literal interpolation renders as 'a,b'; nested ternaries parse; bool() accepts the module's native boolean values. While a variable is undefined / 'ERROR' / 'PATH_ERROR', the jsonparse-based texts render 'undefined' rather than an error string.

Control gap: workload start/stop/restart/sync and failover are REST-only (POST /api/session/renderstream/startlayers|stoplayers|restartlayers|synclayers|failover); RenderStreamModuleConfig.startWorkload()/stopWorkload() exist in the pyi but would fire on subscription if placed in a property path, so no control rows are proposed. perDim.verifySummary: The candidate JSON (docs/research/phase0-candidates.json) has no connection/templates dimension (keys: monitoring, transport, track_layer, stage, exprvars, renderstream, failover), so every row correctly cites only "module:connectionState" or "template"; all strings were checked against src/feedbacks.ts, src/actions.ts, src/index.ts, src/variables.ts, src/presets.ts, docs/INVENTORY.md and docs/PRESET_CATALOG_RULES.md. Ids (conn_, tpl_) are unique and prefixed correctly, names are <= 40 chars, the 11 template rows share one pair (<OBJECT_PATH>, object.<PROPERTY_PATH>) with one variable name (myValue) and one freqClass (state), action option ids are exactly variableName/value (toggle takes variableName only, matching extension 4), Boolean values are real booleans, Number values are valid JS expressions, the JSON value parses, every textTemplate uses only existing expression functions (toFixed, jsonparse, jsonpath) and references $(liveupdate:myValue) of its own row, previewText and liveTestPriority are present on every row, no experimental rows exist and no candidate of status unverified/reject is used. Concrete defects found: (1) tpl_set_number.range and the tpl_setup text claim Infinity is rejected, but processNumberValue only checks typeof number && !isNaN, so Infinity passes (src/actions.ts:60-63); (2) previewText of tpl_watch_json / tpl_set_json shows 0.50 but jsonpath returns the raw number 0.5, so the button renders "0.5"; (3) conn_status understates the connectionState hazard: ws 'close' never calls checkFeedbacks() and no Director message arrives while disconnected, so the button stays GREEN with the text "Disconnected" for the whole outage, and after a connect it stays red until a subscriptions/valuesChanged message, which never comes on a page without any liveUpdateVariable feedback (src/index.ts:399-421, 556, 654); (4) the placeholder-guard description in tpl_setup omits the "$NA" and unparsed "$(" conditions from RULES §4 and the "PATH_ERROR (unsubscribed)" 3-strike variant; (5) nudge rows must state that the generator sets options.rotaryActions: true, otherwise rotate_left/rotate_right sets are inert; (6) the "wrap=false" jsonpath claim in tpl_watch_json notes is not verifiable from the local sources (the companion_api research text only confirms the function exists) and should be softened. Advisory for the lead (not a row failure): INVENTORY §5 records that the module never parses $(custom:...) in path options while RULES §4 relies on host-side parsing since module API 1.13; conn_setup repeats the RULES claim, which is fine if the lead's rule stands but should be confirmed in Phase 3. The draft's use of "object.<PROPERTY_PATH>" (RULES §4 says "<PROPERTY_PATH>") is acceptable because every property path must start with "object." and the literal placeholder is preserved. No missing rows: the module exposes nothing else natively; an optional "Watch: seconds as timecode" template would be a convenience, not a coverage gap.

critic.summary: Cross-category review of 8 dimension drafts (254 normal rows, 127 experimental rows, 16 text presets). Structural findings: one preset-id collision (conn_setup emitted by both failover and connection_templates), one hard variable-name conflict on a shared pair (Machine:"$(custom:d3_machine)" / object.hasTakenOverFailedMachine() is machineTakenOver in 10 Failover and machineHasTakenOver in 09 RenderStream), one custom-variable semantic overload (d3_layer means a timeline layer in 05/06 but an ExpressionVariables layer in ev_layer_vars), and one case-only near-collision (trackname vs trackName). The operator must create 21 d3_* custom variables (13 for normal-tier rows, 8 more for experimental rows); the conn_setup text lists only 11 of them and the fo/rs/monr setup texts describe d3_machine with three different definitions. OSC parity: trackname, volume, brightness and playMode ship at normal tier; currentSectionName, nextSectionName, sectionElapsed, sectionRemaining, bpm, trackposition and timecodeposition exist only as experimental (inferred) rows, and the two section-time rows report BEATS while the OSC module reports seconds. Essentials still missing after the verifiers' missingRows: current-track length (tr-22), UID-path renderLayer/isInError for LED walls, projector isInActiveStage, a normal-tier playhead-in-seconds (none doc-verified, so only a live-test priority), any control in 08 Expression Variables, and the disputed fo-18 NIC adaptor readout. Rule gaps the verifiers missed: doc-verified comprehensions placed in 99 Experimental keep status doc-verified (rule table has no such cell), 99 Experimental heading text presets are inconsistent across dimensions (ids monl_exp_setup/monr_exp_setup/trk_x_setup/stg_experimental_setup/ev_x_setup, none with homeCategory, and transport/renderstream/failover/connection ship none), and several rows use freqClass playhead on non-transport values without a visible freqRationale. After applying the per-dimension verifier removals (6 stage offset Y/Z rows, ev_uid_knob) and merging the duplicate takeover row, the catalog is 246 normal + 127 experimental rows.

Keep the connection_templates version (category owner) and fold the failover text's list of experimental conn_* ids (conn_session_name, conn_project_name, conn_designer_version, conn_designer_version_name, conn_licence_days, conn_in_show) into it.

Different pairs so the rule is satisfied, but Companion variable ids differing only by case are a support hazard and tr's name is fixed by OSC parity. An operator who sets d3_layer = 'Video 1' for 06 Layer Control gets a PATH_ERROR (and 3-strike unsubscribe) on the EV row. Rename the EV row's variable to d3_evlayer.
